title: Sequential vs. Simultaneous Actions
use_cases: Use when describing a complex series of physical movements
Configure when rhythmic clutter obscures the reader's visualization
Implement when transitioning between distinct character reactions
Use when correcting physically impossible simultaneous actions
content:
A key insight about prose rhythm is understanding that readers process information sequentially, not simultaneously. When you write, “Shaking his head, he turned, walking away, mumbling something about wasting his time,” you’re suggesting all these actions happen at once—which is both physically impossible and rhythmically cluttered.

Instead, create a clear sequence:

He turned and walked away, shaking his head. Then he slammed the office door.

This approach gives each action its own beat, allowing the reader to visualize the sequence clearly.
